 Glossary
memory cells—lymphocytes produced on the ﬁ rst encounter
with an antigen that produce a rapid, more vigorous response 
upon subsequent exposures, which often prevents reinfection
menhaden oil—hydrogenated and partially hydrogenated oils 
from the menhaden ﬁ sh (a small plankton-feeding ﬁ sh)
metabolic acidosis—condition resulting from either loss of 
bicarbonate or retention of nonvolatile acid
metabolic alkalosis—condition resulting from either retention
of bicarbonate or loss of nonvolatile acid
metabolic decompensation—an inability to maintain meta-
bolic balance leading to derangements in biochemical and
clinical parameters
metabolic water—water that is produced through nutrient 
metabolism
metabolomics—study of the collection of all metabolites pres-
ent in a living organism
metaplasia—replacement of one cell type with another
metastasis—spread of cancer from the primary site to nearby 
or distant areas through the blood or lymph
methylation—the addition of methyl (-CH3) groups; DNA 
methylation patterns can be inherited and impact patterns of 
gene expression
microalbuminuria—the leaking of small amounts of albumin 
into the urine by the kidneys
microarray—technology used to measure expression of thou-
sands of genes simultaneously
